messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: dedpool-gpu-07 parity/psu-intermittent errors detected on dedicated-pool 'aurora-reserved-3' (customer: NovaGen, VPC). Current state: node gpu-07 rejecting new allocations, kernel logs show repeated PCIe parity errors. Suggested action: immediate isolate/drain + hardware ticket. Severity: P1 -> P2 if mitigated 
amy (oncall-sre): on it. pinging infra and account team. I'll take ownership for initial mitigation.
amy (oncall-sre): @javier can you confirm whether this node is on spot-backed hosts or reserved? need to know eviction policy before we drain.
javier (eng-infra): it's on a reserved chassis but the GPU card is on a PSU rail that's shared across two sockets. not spot. parity errors look intermittent — kernel oops x3 in 2hrs.
kim (platform-eng): seeing tail of kernel log: ``[ 12543.211] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple parity/unmasked error`` also the controller reset loop at 12548s. GPU process restarts for tenants observed.
michelle (acct-se): cc @ben from NovaGen ops — customer reported increased latency and intermittent 500s on some inferences. They are on dedicated VPC; we must coordinate live migration.
ben (customer-ops): Confirmed. Two inference routes (lambda-embed, chat-completions) spiking errors 10:12-10:18 UTC. Customer requests minimal downtime window, prefer graceful migration.
amy (oncall-sre): Plan: 1) Isolate node (remove from scheduler) 2) Drain running containers/tenants with migration to reserve pool 3) Pin critical NovaGen jobs to fallback pool + enable routing fallback 4) Open hardware replace ticket with vendor 5) Postmortem. Any objections?
javier (eng-infra): ACK. I'll run cordon+evacuate. commands: ```kubectl cordon gpu-07 && kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force``` note: there are long-lived KV cache pods for rerank workers — we should migrate cache or accept cold start.
kim (platform-eng): also temporarily toggle automatic routing fallback for NovaGen to allow spill -> ``/api/v1/routing/tenants/NOVA/fallback?enable=true`` will coordinate with console team.
amy (oncall-sre): Michelle, can you confirm which NovaGen routes are critical and which can be throttled? list of tenants?
michelle (acct-se): Critical: chat-completions-prod, embed-live-prod. Non-critical: batch-analytics. I'll get list and an agreed window.
ben (customer-ops): We prefer a rolling migration now. We'll accept transient cold caches but cannot have >10s tail latency for chat.
amy (oncall-sre): Noted. Javier — start drain in 3 minutes. Kim — prepare fallback routing and set low-latency priority for chat-completions to reserve pool.
javier (eng-infra): Starting drain now. Pushing eviction signals to tenants. Logs: ``evicting pod/novagen-chat-7 -> graceful timeout 45s``
ops-bot: Deploy job started: dedpool/evacuation/gpu-07 by javier at 1723456801. Steps: cordon -> drain -> detach -> hw-ticket.
amy (oncall-sre): Observing migration. chat-completions pods recreating on reserve host pool aurora-hot-1. Live metrics show 30% decreased throughput during restart but no hard 500s so far.
kim (platform-eng): Routing fallback toggled for NovaGen: enabled. Confirmed traffic spill to aurora-hot-1. Also set rate limit bump to allow warmup: ``rate_limit: +20% for chat-completions-prod``
michelle (acct-se): Notified NovaGen that we're performing live migration and that some calls may see cold-starts. They asked for probe URL to confirm readiness.
ben (customer-ops): spinning up health-check probes now. metrics look green for embeds. chat p99 at 1.8s currently (was spike to 6s earlier).
amy (oncall-sre): Drain progress: 8/10 tenant pods evacuated, 2 remaining (long-lived KV caches). Javier, those two are stateful; what's status?
javier (eng-infra): KV caches pinned to local NVMe. Migration requires cache warmup on reserve, which will take ~2-3m. Options: 1) force delete (risk data loss), 2) live dataset rsync + restart, 3) accept cold cache. Recommend option 3 for safety.
amy (oncall-sre): agree accept cold cache. Notify customer. Kim, can we prioritize cache warmups by allocating burst CPU for cache-loader jobs?
kim (platform-eng): yes, bumping CPU share on aurora-hot-1 for cache-loader jobs. kicking prefetch job: ``/ops/cache/prefetch --tenant NOVA --target aurora-hot-1``
ops-bot: Prefetch job queued (job-id 8f3a). ETA warmup ~150s.
michelle (acct-se): NovaGen OK with cold cache if we can keep p99 < 10s. They're watching.
amy (oncall-sre): Drain complete. Node isolated. hw-ticket opened with vendor, ticket# VND-88122, technician visit ETA 8 hours. Marking node offline and replacing GPU card on site.
javier (eng-infra): Node removed from pool and marked needs-replace. Updating inventory -> slot reserved. Will schedule replacement during maintenance window if vendor cannot expedite.
kim (platform-eng): Routing policy left in fallback ON for 30m then we'll progressively revert when metrics stable. Also enabled automatic rollback to original host if drain shows degradation.
ben (customer-ops): Confirming NovaGen sees stable behavior. No 500s for 10m. Thank you team.
amy (oncall-sre): Post-incident actions: - hw RCA with vendor - add parity-error alert with earlier threshold - update runbook to include KV cache migration guidance - pre-warm reserve pools for heavy VPC customers
michelle (acct-se): I'll draft customer communication and post the timeline.
amy (oncall-sre): Closing on-call handoff to javier for follow-up tasks (inventory, replacement scheduling) and to michelle for customer comms. If anything degrades, page oncall. :white_check_mark: 
ops-bot: Incident P2 acknowledged closed for active mitigation. Follow-ups assigned: javier (hw-replace), kim (routing rollback plan), michelle (customer comm).
